headline: High: shared git/workspace and permissive tool use create dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways between Aider and Cursor.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a git repo, while Cursor can ingest workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard contents. That creates a plausible file-based instruction bridge even without a browser or MCP on Aider. The pathway is not as direct as raw web content, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Aider writes attacker-controlled instructions into a repo file that Cursor opens
IF Cursor treats workspace text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic agent execution on files in the shared repo
Use a dedicated non-shared workspace for one agent
Add a manual review step before Cursor follows repo text
Restrict Cursor clipboard ingestion during pair runs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and open files, and both have broad network egress to model providers. Cursor additionally exposes clipboard contents and workspace files, while Aider shares state through the git repo. Sensitive code or secrets can therefore flow from one agent’s workspace into the other’s prompts or outputs in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared repo or editor buffers
IF either agent forwards file contents to its model provider during normal operation
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo
Run both agents on a scrubbed test branch
Disable clipboard-based transfer between tools
Limit each agent to a separate checkout
Review outbound prompts for file content before sending

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared git-repo state; Cursor has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared state via local filesystem, plus Yolo mode can auto-run terminal commands. Both can mutate the same repo concurrently without an explicit locking primitive in the profiles, so conflicting writes and git-state corruption are a default danger.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same branch or working tree concurrently
IF no external lock or serialized handoff is enforced
mitigations: Assign one agent per branch
Serialize edits with a simple lock file
Require git status clean before each handoff
Turn off Cursor Yolo mode during shared-repo work
Use separate clones for parallel tasks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces git commits and Cursor runs a multi-step agent loop with tool use; Cursor can treat Aider’s edits or commit messages as authoritative inputs. Because both can act on code changes directly, an error in Aider can cascade into Cursor applying, extending, or shipping it without a strong verification barrier.
conditions: IF Cursor consumes Aider-produced diffs or commit messages as trusted context
IF Cursor auto-applies follow-up edits without independent validation
mitigations: Require Cursor to diff-review Aider commits before acting
Add a human approval checkpoint between agents
Use tests or linting before any follow-up edit
Limit Aider to proposing patches, not committing them
Disable auto-run for Cursor tool calls on shared tasks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not specify regulated-data certifications, residency, or retention mismatches. The only concrete compliance-relevant difference is Cursor’s clipboard and cloud/API surfaces versus Aider’s git-repo workflow, which could matter for sensitive code handling, but the profiles do not prove a specific residency or certification breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cursor clipboard or cloud-synced buffers
IF an operator requires a residency or retention guarantee not stated in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workspace
Check vendor privacy docs before use
Use local-only test data for pair runs
Disable clipboard transfer for sensitive sessions
